from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Matrices are functions transforming inputs into outputs.",
            "A 2D vector gets mapped by a 2x2 matrix.",
            "Transformation means rotation, scaling, or shearing."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Refresher: The Mapping Perspective", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a vector space R^2. (Color: #FFFFFF)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E3")
        vector = Vector([1, 2], color=WHITE)
        self.add(axes, vector)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(axes), GrowArrow(vector))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent the mapping as an arrow from R^n to R^m. (Color: #FF8080)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF8080")
        target_axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(target_axes, "B4", "E6")
        mapping_arrow = Arrow(start=RIGHT*1, end=LEFT*1, color="#FF8080").shift(UP*1.2)
        mapping_label = Text("T", color="#FF8080").next_to(mapping_arrow, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(target_axes), FadeIn(mapping_arrow), Write(mapping_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualize the domain R^n and codomain R^m separately. (Color: #80FF80)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#80FF80")
        new_vector = Vector([2, -1], color="#80FF80")
        new_vector.move_to(target_axes.c2p(2, -1))
        
        self.play(Transform(vector.copy(), new_vector), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Expanding Dimensions (m > n)", [
            "Embedding maps low to high dimensions.",
            "Think of a 2D plane in 3D space.",
            "Information is stretched, not destroyed."
        ])
        
        # Assets for animation
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Compressing Dimensions (m < n)", [
            "Projection collapses high to low dimensions.",
            "Imagine casting a 3D shadow onto 2D.",
            "Information is lost during this compression."
        ])
        
        # Visual elements
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        plane = Square(side_length=2, fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_width=2, color=BLUE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Projection collapses high to low dimensions.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(cube, 'B2')
        self.play(Create(cube))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Imagine casting a 3D shadow onto 2D.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF8080")
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'B5')
        shadow = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.5, fill_opacity=0.5, color=RED)
        shadow.move_to(plane.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(cube, shadow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Information is lost during this compression.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#80FF80")
        loss_text = Text("Loss of depth", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(loss_text, 'E3')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(loss_text))
        self.play(Indicate(shadow))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the 'Null Space' Loss", [
            "Null space represents information lost in projection.",
            "Some inputs map directly to zero.",
            "This is the cost of dimensionality reduction."
        ])
        
        # 1. Null space representation
        null_space_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(null_space_rect, "B2", "C3")
        label_null = Text("Null Space", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        label_null.next_to(null_space_rect, UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(null_space_rect), Write(label_null))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # 2. Animate vectors mapping to zero
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#FF8080")
        self.place_at_grid(vector, "E3")
        target_point = Dot(self.grid["F4"], color="#FF8080")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(vector))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF8080")
        self.play(vector.animate.move_to(target_point.get_center()), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Collapse effect
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#80FF80")
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "B5")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#80FF80")
        self.play(circle.animate.scale(0.1).set_opacity(0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Non-square matrices connect different dimensions.", "They act as either embeddings or projections.", "These tools are vital for data science."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a grid summarizing transformation types.
        grid_group = VGroup()
        for pos in ["B2", "B3", "B4", "C2", "C3", "C4"]:
            dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
            self.place_at_grid(dot, pos)
            grid_group.add(dot)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_group))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash key concepts like 'Expansion' and 'Compression'.
        label1 = Text("Expansion", font_size=20, color="#FF8080")
        label2 = Text("Compression", font_size=20, color="#FF8080")
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "A3")
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "D3")
        self.play(FadeIn(label1), FadeIn(label2))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF8080"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show the final mapping diagram overlay.
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["B2"], end=self.grid["C4"], color="#80FF80")
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#80FF80"))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices as Dimensional Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Mapping Perspective
sections.content: Define a matrix not just as a grid of numbers, but as a function f(x) = Ax. Emphasize that a vector input undergoes a 'transformation' to become a new output vector.
sections.example: Visualize a 2D arrow (vector) being rotated and stretched on a 2D plane by a 2x2 matrix.

sections.title: Expanding Dimensions (m > n)
sections.content: Explain how an n x m matrix with m > n acts as an embedding function. It takes a lower-dimensional object and maps it into a higher-dimensional space, essentially 'stretching' the object into a thin plane or line within the larger room.
sections.example: A 2D 'Flat Cat' character moving through a 3D 'Shadow Caster' machine (a 3x2 matrix) that projects the cat into 3D space as a floating paper cutout.

sections.title: Compressing Dimensions (m < n)
sections.content: Explain the reverse process: m < n acts as a projection. It collapses high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional subspace, similar to how a light source casts a shadow.
sections.example: A 3D 'Robot' model being passed through a 2x3 matrix, resulting in a 2D silhouette (shadow) on the wall; information is preserved on the plane but lost in the depth axis.

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Null Space' Loss
sections.content: Discuss the 'Compression Loss' concept. When projecting to lower dimensions, some directions in the original space are collapsed to the origin (zero), representing information that cannot be recovered.
sections.example: A 3D 'spinning top' where all vertical heights are crushed to zero by the transformation, leaving only a 2D circular path.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Non-square matrices are bridges between dimensions. They either 'embed' (up-dimension) or 'project' (down-dimension).
sections.example: The 'Data Lens' analogy: A camera lens (matrix) takes a 3D scene (world) and maps it to a 2D image (sensor), showcasing the power of non-square transformation in data reduction.
